lobule.sinusoid_transit_source: 教科书量级，非本项目计算
lobule.bile_direction: canaliculus -> bile ductule at the portal tract (outward, counter-current to the blood)

respiration.parenchymal_deformation: none — the liver is displaced, not deformed
respiration.source: 由本项目心率模型拟合的呼吸性窦性心律不齐频率导出（PhysioNet nsrdb/16265 公开数据）

perCell.sampling: per-cell-type reservoir sampling (Algorithm R) over the full contiguous-block stream of every liver cell in the Census; quota = clip(round(80 + 0.004*n_cells_of_type), 40, 600)

plate_cutaway.reason: the front hepatic plate is hidden so the sinusoid, its endothelial lining, the Kupffer and stellate cells and the canaliculus are visible from outside; the same device as the lobule tier 60-degree sector

cellTier.composition_source: published human-liver cell-NUMBER shares (hepatocyte 60%, sinusoidal endothelium 20%, Kupffer 15%, stellate 5%)
cellTier.microvillus_density: SCHEMATIC — height is real (0.5 um), surface density is not taken from any measurement
cellTier.fenestrae: NOT RENDERED — sinusoidal endothelial fenestrae are 50-150 nm, below this tier's rendered resolution; the lining is drawn as a continuous sheet
cellTier.scaling_claim: 610 cells are rendered. An adult human liver holds of the order of 2e11 hepatocytes. A rendered cell does NOT stand for a block of real cells: it IS the one Census cell that was sampled, and its gene values are that cell's own measurements.

candidates_tried: endothelial cell of pericentral hepatic sinusoid
endothelial cell of periportal hepatic sinusoid

perCellVerify.note: the panel recomputes CP10K-log1p in the browser from each cell's own raw counts and raw_sum; this compares that result against the value stored in liver_cells.json for the same cell and gene

geneTint.scale: per-instance colour = that one Census cell's own CP10K-log1p for this gene, divided by the maximum over the rendered hepatocytes

respirationAudit.note: two points on the cut face, 97.7 mm apart, were tracked over one breath. Their separation is preserved to the drift figure above, which is what a rigid translation+rotation does and what any resizing could not do. Their DISPLACEMENT VECTORS differ by up to the second figure, which is the signature of the real 2.2 deg rotation about the hepatocaval confluence — a pure translation would make that number zero. The face therefore travels WITH the organ, rotation included, and nothing in the scene is being scaled.

capping.method: two-pass stencil (back faces increment, front faces decrement), cap quad painted only where stencil != 0
capping.depth_fight_handling: polygonOffset per cap, no geometric displacement

cap.interpretation: cap_on renders ONLY the cut face, viewed down the plane normal with an orthographic camera of known scale, so its implied area should match cpu_mesh_slice_area_mm2 — a number computed on the CPU by intersecting the 137k-triangle parenchyma with the same plane and applying the shoelace formula, which never touches the GPU. solid_only re-renders the clipped solid with the cap hidden: that is what an UNCAPPED cut looks like from the same viewpoint, and the two areas being different is the whole point of capping.

frame_budget.note: fpsMean is NOT by itself a user-visible frame rate, so the per-frame render cost and the p95 frame time are reported against the 16.67 ms 60-fps budget instead. Headless Chromium CAN run rAF uncapped, in which case the fps figure is meaningless. vsync_detected is set from THIS viewport's own measurement (per-frame cost within 0.2 ms of the 16.67 ms presentation interval). It is true here: the frame times are pinned to the display refresh, so they are a FLOOR at 60 fps and say nothing about how much headroom remains. The p95 is the 95th percentile of a 0.1 ms-quantised histogram, so viewports that are equally vsynced can still differ by one bin.
